title: Generic varargs that keep the @SafeVarargs promise

blocks.text: `@SafeVarargs` is a promise: this generic varargs method only reads its array and never lets it escape, so callers need no heap-pollution warning. It fits only methods that cannot be overridden: `static`, `final`, `private` methods and constructors. The page's safe example copies the elements into a new list.
Write `Varargs` with two methods that **carry `@SafeVarargs`** and keep the promise:

items: `static <T> List<T> listOf(T... elements)`: the elements in order, in a list that **does not share the varargs array**. **`null` elements are kept.**
`final <T> List<List<T>> group(T[]... arrays)`: one list per array, in order, each **a copy of its array**.

rows: the list still starts with the old element

cases.says: listOf("a", "b", "c") gives [a, b, c] and group of two arrays gives one list per array, in order.
Changing the array passed to listOf() afterwards does not change the list it returned.
Changing one of the arrays passed to group() afterwards does not change its list.
Reflection finds @SafeVarargs on listOf() and on group(), because it has RUNTIME retention.

concepts: @SafeVarargs promises that a generic varargs method only reads its array and never lets it escape, as a method that copies the elements does.
